modules.title: Targeting applications
modules.body: Distinguish a programme commencing in several years from a current vacancy. Read mandatory requirements before preferences, record the published application route and select roles that fit your actual experience.
modules.exercise: Choose three adverts; classify each requirement as mandatory, desirable or unclear. Record evidence or a question for each.
modules.scenario: A candidate with a law degree sees a vacancy requiring two years of paralegal experience. They have three months of internship experience. What should they do?
options: Treat the two-year requirement as met because the degree is relevant
Check whether the wording permits equivalents; target genuinely suitable roles and avoid misrepresenting experience
Claim the internship was two years
modules.explanation: A law degree does not establish a specified period of work. A transparent application may be appropriate if the employer explicitly allows equivalent experience.

modules.title: Eligibility and right to work
modules.body: Right to work now and eligibility for employer-sponsored work later are distinct. A sponsor licence is not evidence of support for a particular vacancy. Use official immigration rules and ask recruiters about the precise role.
modules.exercise: Create a timeline of current permission and future requirements without recording passport or visa numbers.
modules.scenario: An employer appears on the sponsor register. Does that prove it will sponsor a paralegal vacancy?
options: No, check role-specific policy and current immigration requirements
Only if the vacancy is permanent
modules.explanation: A licence is a necessary organisational capability for many sponsorship routes, not an individual commitment.

modules.title: Firm differentiation
modules.body: Differentiate firms using actual practice work, client relationships and strategy. A deal attribution demonstrates a mandate, not necessarily a firm-wide strength. Combine evidence of work with genuine personal motivation.
modules.exercise: Compare two firm profiles; explain one meaningful difference using named mandates and an honest connection to your interests.
modules.scenario: Which is the strongest reason for applying?
options: A specific mandate, what interests you about the legal work, and how it relates to your experience
modules.explanation: Specific evidence plus genuine motivation is more informative than generic prestige language.

modules.title: CV evidence
modules.body: Use clear action, legal or business context and the real output. Distinguish observed, assisted, researched, drafted, reviewed and led. Never invent results or authority.
modules.exercise: Rewrite two truthful experience statements; check the verbs against what you actually did.
modules.scenario: You checked a draft agreement under supervision. Which wording is accurate?
options: Reviewed draft agreement clauses and flagged issues for supervisor
modules.explanation: The third answer reflects the actual contribution and preserves the supervision boundary.

modules.title: Competency examples
modules.body: Use a concise situation, task, action and result structure. Focus on your own contribution, decisions, lessons and verifiable outcomes.
modules.exercise: Build three examples covering teamwork, accuracy and prioritisation. Record what you would improve next time.
modules.scenario: What makes a teamwork example strongest?
options: A detailed team achievement without your contribution
Your specific actions, how you worked with others and the actual outcome
A hypothetical answer presented as fact
modules.explanation: The example should establish your behaviour, not simply the group's result.

modules.title: Interview motivation
modules.body: Connect the role to informed interests and relevant personal evidence. For paralegal jobs show understanding of the day-to-day work, not only ambition to qualify.
modules.exercise: Record a 90-second response for why this role and why this employer.
modules.scenario: What is a strong answer for a legal support role?
options: Only say you want a future training contract
Explain how accurate support, document work and client service interest you, with relevant evidence
modules.explanation: Recruiters need evidence of motivation for the actual position.

modules.title: Feedback and rejection
modules.body: Recruitment outcomes have multiple possible explanations. Use actual feedback and observable patterns rather than assuming the ATS or a protected characteristic caused rejection.
modules.exercise: Review your last five applications by stage and record one testable improvement for the next cycle.
modules.scenario: Three employers reject you without explanation. What can you establish?
options: All used the same scoring rule
Your CV is definitely the only cause
Only the outcomes; examine eligibility, targeting and writing and seek feedback where available
modules.explanation: Avoid unsupported causal claims. Review evidence and test a specific change.

modules.title: Written client advice
modules.body: Lead with the answer and key uncertainty, separate facts from analysis, specify a practical next step and use plain language. Do not overpromise a legal conclusion.
modules.exercise: Draft a 150-word client email from a fictional problem and revise for actionability.
modules.scenario: What should a short client email put first?
options: A long history of the law
The issue, practical recommendation and important caveat
modules.explanation: A useful email helps the client decide, while respecting uncertainties and scope.

modules.title: Research method
modules.body: Begin with the issue and jurisdiction, find primary legislation or regulator guidance, verify date and application, then explain facts and caveats. Secondary commentary can help locate sources.
modules.exercise: Research a narrow question using an official source and document the exact section and date.
modules.scenario: A blog contradicts current official rules. What next?
options: Read the current primary source and reconcile scope/date before advising
modules.explanation: Authority, currency and applicability matter more than search rank.

modules.title: Document control
modules.body: Track version, author, recipient, changes and confidentiality. Check comparison direction and verify the clean copy reflects agreed edits.
modules.exercise: Compare two fictional versions of a clause; log the change and flag the version used.
modules.scenario: A revised contract arrives just before execution. What is safest?
options: Compare to agreed version, escalate unexpected changes and verify approval
Assume file name proves it is agreed
modules.explanation: Execution readiness requires a reliable version history and approval.

modules.title: Prioritisation
modules.body: Clarify deadline, impact, dependency and scope. Escalate conflicts early with a proposed sequence; communicate accurately rather than promising impossible timing.
modules.exercise: Prioritise three tasks with different deadlines and commercial consequences.
modules.scenario: Two supervisors assign urgent work due at the same time. What should you do?
options: Confirm priorities with the supervisors, give realistic timing and propose a plan
modules.explanation: Early communication and prioritisation preserve quality and trust.

modules.title: Confidentiality
modules.body: Do not send client material to an unapproved service or use real client information in training exercises. Report potential data exposure using the organisation's policy.
modules.exercise: Identify what must be redacted from a fictional document before training use.
modules.scenario: Can you upload a confidential client SPA to a public AI tool for convenience?
options: Yes if no one sees you
Only if you delete it afterward
No without approved policy, authority and safeguards
modules.explanation: Confidential information requires authorised systems and appropriate safeguards.

modules.title: Commercial numeracy
modules.body: Distinguish margin, growth, multiples and percentage points. Always identify the denominator, units and timeframe before interpreting a calculation.
modules.exercise: Calculate revenue growth and EBITDA margin for a fictional company; explain why neither proves cash flow.
modules.scenario: Revenue rises from £80m to £100m. What is the growth rate?

modules.title: Critical reasoning
modules.body: A conclusion must be supported by the stated premises. Separate necessary inference from plausible assumptions and evaluate the argument, not your prior opinion.
modules.exercise: Read a short factual paragraph and list what is certain, possible and unsupported.
modules.scenario: All approved transactions require a signature. A transaction has a signature. Is it necessarily approved?
options: No; signature may be necessary but not sufficient
modules.explanation: The conditional does not establish its converse.

modules.title: Group exercise
modules.body: Contribute substance, listen, invite quieter participants and help the group make a reasoned decision under time pressure. Do not dominate or withdraw.
modules.exercise: Discuss a fictional acquisition with a partner; summarise options and propose a decision.
modules.scenario: Two group members disagree on a recommendation. Best action?
options: Identify shared criteria, test both options and agree a next step
modules.explanation: Useful collaboration turns disagreement into a reasoned comparison.

modules.title: Video interview
modules.body: Practise aloud, use a clear structure and check employer rules about recording, notes and AI. Never use unauthorised assistance during an assessment.
modules.exercise: Record a local practice answer independently; assess structure and specificity.
modules.scenario: A firm prohibits AI during its assessment. What should you do?
options: Ask AI to answer in real time
Follow the employer rule; use independent preparation beforehand
modules.explanation: Respect the exact assessment conditions.

modules.title: Networking
modules.body: Ask focused, respectful questions about work and recruitment. Personalise outreach without requesting confidential information or assuming a referral.
modules.exercise: Draft a brief message asking for insight into a practice area, then plan one polite follow-up.
modules.scenario: What is appropriate in a first outreach?
options: Ask a concise question connected to the person's public work
modules.explanation: A specific, respectful request reduces burden and respects boundaries.

modules.title: Qualifying experience
modules.body: For ordinary SQE candidates, QWE is assessed against SRA requirements and needs confirmation; a job title is not enough. Qualified lawyers have a different route.
modules.exercise: Maintain a non-confidential log of work, competencies and potential confirmer; verify eligibility with the SRA.
modules.scenario: Does a virtual simulation automatically count as QWE?
options: No, assess the regulatory requirements; a simulation is not automatically qualifying experience
modules.explanation: QWE depends on legal-services experience and regulatory confirmation, not a badge.

modules.title: In-house counsel mindset
modules.body: Understand the product, customer, revenue and operating constraints. Frame legal risks in business terms, provide options and escalate decisions appropriately.
modules.exercise: Write a brief recommendation about a fictional vendor contract.
modules.scenario: Which response best helps a commercial team?
options: Identify material risk, options, business consequences and approval required
modules.explanation: In-house support connects legal risk to a practical business decision.

modules.title: Legal operations
modules.body: Use structured matter information, ownership, deadlines and status. Measure turnaround carefully; speed alone is not quality. Avoid putting sensitive matter details into unapproved tools.
modules.exercise: Build a fictional matter table with owner, next action and deadline.
modules.scenario: Which is a useful operations metric?
options: Turnaround by request type alongside quality and rework
modules.explanation: Contextual metrics help identify bottlenecks without rewarding poor quality.

modules.title: Negotiation
modules.body: Identify interests, alternatives, authority and trade-offs. Distinguish positions from underlying commercial needs and document unresolved points accurately.
modules.exercise: Prepare three issues, alternatives and possible concessions for a fictional SPA negotiation.
modules.scenario: A seller wants a lower liability cap. What is a useful first step?
options: Understand risk allocation, price, insurance and buyer alternatives
modules.explanation: A cap is part of overall risk allocation; concessions should be considered in context.

modules.title: Professional judgement
modules.body: Do not conceal errors. Protect confidentiality, report concerns promptly and seek supervision when outside competence. Check applicable professional rules and firm policy.
modules.exercise: Describe how you would report an accidental drafting error and propose mitigation.
modules.scenario: You find a material mistake after a draft was sent. What should you do?
options: Immediately tell the supervisor, identify impact and propose correction
modules.explanation: Prompt escalation and correction are safer than concealment.

questions.prompt: A price falls from £120 to £90. Percentage decline?
questions.explanation: 30/120=25%; use original price.

questions.prompt: Revenue £150m, EBITDA £30m. EBITDA margin?
Debt £60m and cash £15m. Net debt, ignoring other items?
questions.explanation: Net debt is debt less cash.

questions.prompt: Equity £120m plus net debt £30m. Simplified EV?
questions.explanation: EV equals equity plus net debt in the simplified model.

questions.prompt: A 400MW battery can deliver power for 3 hours at full rating. Nominal energy?
questions.explanation: Power multiplied by duration gives energy.

questions.prompt: A facility commitment is £80m; £50m drawn. Undrawn amount?
questions.explanation: Commitment minus drawn = 30; availability may depend on terms.

questions.prompt: A margin rises from 10% to 13%. Increase in percentage points?
questions.explanation: 13−10=3 percentage points; relative increase is 30%.

questions.prompt: An offer pays 90p cash plus a 5p dividend. Total shareholder amount?
questions.explanation: Total is 95p; bidder cash is only 90p.

questions.prompt: A £12m loan bears 5% annual simple interest. Annual interest?
A company has 80m shares and issues 20m new shares. New investor's share of enlarged capital?
Every eligible applicant has a degree. Maya has a degree. Is she necessarily eligible?
questions.explanation: Necessary does not imply sufficient.

questions.prompt: No deal may close before regulatory approval. Approval has been obtained. Must it close?
questions.explanation: Other conditions and decisions may remain.

questions.prompt: A release says expected synergies of £20m. What follows?
questions.explanation: Expectation is not an achieved outcome.

questions.prompt: A firm represented a lender on one acquisition. What is established?
questions.explanation: The specific client and role only.

questions.prompt: A published deadline has passed. What is established?
options: Published deadline passed; check for extensions
questions.explanation: An elapsed deadline does not establish any extension or individual status.

questions.prompt: Two websites reproduce the same issuer release. Independent corroboration?
questions.explanation: Different domains do not establish independent evidence.

questions.prompt: A target is described as profitable; no financial data given. Can EBITDA margin be calculated?
questions.explanation: No revenue or EBITDA amounts.

questions.prompt: A conditional offer is announced. Can completion be asserted?
questions.explanation: Announcement is distinct from completion.

questions.prompt: A release says the buyer may raise additional debt. Does it say the buyer has drawn it?
questions.explanation: May raise is not actual drawing.

questions.prompt: A report gives projected capacity in development. Which statement is supported?
options: Capacity is planned, not necessarily operating
questions.explanation: Development status is distinct from operational capacity.

questions.prompt: The application says experience desirable. Is it explicitly mandatory?
questions.explanation: Desirable is not the same as mandatory; confirm other criteria.

questions.prompt: A company says it intends to preserve jobs. What is established?
questions.explanation: An intention is not necessarily an enforceable undertaking.

questions.prompt: A role is hybrid; no days specified. What can you infer?
options: Office location and schedule unknown unless stated
questions.explanation: Do not invent attendance frequency.

questions.prompt: A supervisor gives a task beyond your competence. Best action?
options: Explain limits and ask for guidance
questions.explanation: Seek supervision and establish scope.

questions.prompt: You receive a suspicious email requesting client data. Best action?
options: Verify via approved channel and report if appropriate
questions.explanation: Avoid unverified disclosure.

questions.prompt: Two sources disagree on acquisition value. Best action?
options: Reconcile date, basis and scope; flag unresolved difference
questions.explanation: Disagreement may arise from distinct valuation bases.

questions.prompt: A colleague asks you to claim work they performed as yours on an application. Best action?
questions.explanation: Authenticity is necessary.

questions.prompt: A client asks for advice before the supervisor approves it. Best action?
options: Explain timing and obtain appropriate review
questions.explanation: Respect supervision and authority.

questions.prompt: A hearing deadline conflicts with an internal research task. Best action?
options: Confirm legal deadline and priorities; communicate conflict promptly
questions.explanation: Assess consequences and escalate.

questions.prompt: You find an accessibility issue in a practice test. Best action?
options: Report issue, request reasonable adjustment where appropriate
questions.explanation: Ask relevant provider through appropriate channels.

questions.prompt: A buyer plans to integrate systems; a remedy requires divestment. What matters?
options: Effect on synergies, separability and closing conditions
questions.explanation: Remedy affects strategic value and execution.

questions.prompt: A sponsor uses leverage. What increases vulnerability?
options: Higher debt service with weaker cash flow
questions.explanation: Debt service and cash generation affect resilience.

questions.prompt: A firm advises a borrower on financing. Is it necessarily acting for lenders?
questions.explanation: Mandates are client-specific.

questions.prompt: A £100m grant is awarded subject to eligible spend. Is it £100m cash received today?
questions.explanation: Award, entitlement and disbursement are distinct.

questions.prompt: A buyer acquires 60% of shares. What still needs review?
options: Voting, reserved matters and minority rights
questions.explanation: Ownership percentage alone does not establish governance powers.

questions.prompt: Why distinguish a closing date and delisting date?
questions.explanation: A scheme effective date and trading cancellation can differ.

questions.prompt: Enterprise value £240m, cash £18m, debt £52m and agreed debt-like liabilities £6m. Ignoring other adjustments, equity consideration?
Revenue of £160m rises 10%; EBITDA of £24m falls 12.5%. New EBITDA margin, to one decimal?
A sponsor invests £60m equity and later sells for £180m EV with £70m net debt. Ignore fees and distributions. Equity multiple?
questions.explanation: Exit equity £110m divided by £60m = 1.83x; not an annualised return.

questions.prompt: A regulator accepts undertakings. The bidder states court sanction remains a condition. What is established?
questions.explanation: The two sources address separate conditions.

questions.prompt: Two reports cite a release for £400m consideration. The original offer document says £400m is the maximum including contingent payments. What follows?
options: News reports outweigh the offer document
questions.explanation: Repeated reports share an origin; maximum consideration is not actual payment.

questions.prompt: All shortlisted candidates passed a written test; some passers were not shortlisted. Lina passed. What follows?
questions.explanation: Passing is necessary, not sufficient.

questions.prompt: A fictional notice says a borrower may request an advance by 30 June subject to covenant compliance and no continuing default. What follows?
options: A request alone does not establish entitlement
questions.explanation: The notice specifies conditions and a deadline, not actual funding.

questions.prompt: A fictional vacancy requires a degree before starting, welcomes candidates awaiting results and describes document review experience as desirable. What follows?
options: Candidates awaiting results may apply subject to qualification
questions.explanation: The degree condition remains; desirable experience is not mandatory.

questions.prompt: Management expects £8m annual run-rate savings by year three and £5m implementation costs over two years. What follows?
questions.explanation: Run-rate targets are not cumulative achieved savings or cash flows.

questions.prompt: A diligence summary is due at 4pm. At 2pm you discover material contract schedules are missing. Best response?
options: Wait until 4pm to disclose the gap
Flag promptly and propose conditional summary and follow-up
Substitute terms from a similar contract
questions.explanation: Early escalation allows action and avoids presenting incomplete evidence as verified.

questions.prompt: A filing due today conflicts with an internal research note. Both supervisors assume you are available. Best first step?
options: Confirm external deadline and agree priorities with both
Delegate the filing without checking authority
questions.explanation: Communicate conflicts early and prioritise according to confirmed consequences.

questions.prompt: A colleague suggests uploading a client contract to an unconfirmed external AI service. Best response?
options: Check approved tools and matter restrictions before disclosure
questions.explanation: Confidential terms may remain sensitive even without client names.

questions.prompt: A buyer expects £12m annual synergies, £7m dependent on consolidating units. A remedy requires divesting one. Priority?
options: Treat remedy as unrelated to economics
Reassess synergies, remedy scope, valuation and closing conditions
questions.explanation: The remedy may change operating assumptions; evaluate timing, alternatives and deal terms.

questions.prompt: A SaaS target's largest customer represents 35% of revenue and can terminate on change of control. Priority?
options: Review termination, consent, customer economics and downside valuation
questions.explanation: Concentration and termination create conditional risk, not a guaranteed EBITDA loss.

questions.prompt: A borrower seeks a £100m revolver for seasonal working capital. What best establishes adequacy?
options: Peak cash needs, liquidity, drawdown conditions and covenant headroom
questions.explanation: Usable liquidity depends on timing, cash needs and actual availability.

simulations.title: M&A due diligence
simulations.scenario: Buyer of fictional Atlas Ltd is reviewing three contracts.
simulations.documents: Customer A: 35% of sales; consent required on change of control. Supplier B: terminable on 30 days' notice. Licence C: non-transferable, expires six weeks after closing.
simulations.task: Prepare a three-row red-flag report with severity, impact, proposed mitigation and unresolved facts.
simulations.model: High: consent on Customer A may jeopardise revenue; seek consent/CP or price and risk allocation. Supplier B: continuity risk; negotiate longer notice or alternative sourcing. Licence C: verify whether share sale triggers restriction; secure renewal or transition. Quantify impacts; do not assume consent refusal.
simulations.rubric: Correct clause interpretation; materiality; mitigation; concise caveats.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: SPA risk allocation
simulations.scenario: Fictional buyer discovers £400k tax exposure before signing.
simulations.documents: Draft SPA: general warranties capped at 10% of price; known tax claim excluded from warranties; separate tax covenant not agreed; disclosure letter identifies dispute.
simulations.task: Explain why the buyer should consider a specific indemnity or tax covenant rather than rely solely on warranties.
simulations.model: Known risk may not be recoverable under a disclosed warranty. Consider specific payment protection, scope, exclusions, control of claim, time limits, cap and security. Alternatives include price adjustment or escrow; avoid double recovery.
simulations.rubric: Distinguish known risk and warranty; specific protection; economics; no guaranteed recovery.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Acquisition finance
simulations.documents: Conditions: signed SPA, board approvals, KYC, legal opinions and no specified default. £60m drawn at closing; £40m available subject to conditions.
simulations.task: Create a closing conditions checklist and explain liquidity risk.
simulations.model: List each document, owner, status and deadline. Check actual availability conditions and long-stop date; undrawn commitment is not cash. Escalate missing legal opinion and align SPA completion with drawdown mechanics.
simulations.rubric: Conditions checklist; commitment vs draw; dependencies; escalation.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Debt capital markets
simulations.documents: Coupon benchmark + 150bp; quarterly reset; maturity 2030; senior unsecured; no actual listing notice supplied.
simulations.task: Prepare a one-page note term summary and identify two questions.
simulations.model: Principal £200m, floating interest, quarterly reset, maturity 2030, senior unsecured. Ask benchmark fallback, covenants, redemption, governing law and actual admission. Issuance amount is not enterprise value.
simulations.rubric: Accurate terms; no invented listing; risk questions; plain language.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Competition analysis
simulations.scenario: Two fictional suppliers propose a merger.
simulations.documents: Market A has four significant suppliers; overlapping products; clients report limited switching; no authority decision.
simulations.task: Write a preliminary note on what to investigate, not a definitive clearance prediction.
simulations.model: Define candidate product/geographic markets, market shares, substitution, switching, entry and counterfactual. Assess jurisdictional thresholds and applicable process from current official guidance. Consider potential remedy viability; do not predict outcome.
simulations.rubric: Competition framework; evidence gaps; jurisdiction; uncertainty.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Contract review
simulations.documents: Liability cap equals 3 months' fees; unlimited buyer indemnity; vendor can terminate on 10 days' notice; service levels absent.
simulations.task: Draft three negotiation priorities for a business client.
simulations.model: Assess whether cap is adequate relative to losses and insurance; narrow indemnity scope, third-party claims and fault; improve notice/transition and service commitments. Prioritise continuity and risk proportionality; offer commercial alternatives.
simulations.rubric: Clause identification; commercial consequences; realistic trade-offs; prioritisation.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Private equity rollover
simulations.scenario: Fictional founder sells 70% and reinvests part of proceeds.
simulations.documents: New shares have different voting rights; sponsor preferred return; leaver rules; drag-along provisions; no waterfall provided.
simulations.task: Identify founder-side issues and questions for documents.
simulations.model: Determine rollover valuation and instrument rights, dilution, preference waterfall, leaver pricing, drag/tag and exit. Do not equate headline stake with economic proceeds. Request illustrative exit scenarios and tax advice.
simulations.rubric: Economic vs voting rights; waterfall; exit; open questions.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Corporate approvals
simulations.scenario: Fictional company plans an asset acquisition.
simulations.documents: Board has five directors; one has a disclosed interest; constitutional reserved matters and authority matrix not supplied.
simulations.task: Prepare an approval and signing checklist.
simulations.model: Check articles, board quorum/conflict procedures, reserved matters, delegated signatories, any shareholder/third-party approvals; record resolutions and signing version. Do not assume all approvals required without documents.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Legal research memo
simulations.scenario: A fictional graduate asks whether work as a paralegal always qualifies as QWE.
simulations.documents: Only job title is known; no tasks or confirmer identified. Use official SRA QWE guidance.
simulations.task: Write a 150-word memo separating rule, application and caveat.
simulations.model: No automatic qualification by title. Review whether work provides legal services, develops relevant competencies, duration and confirmation under SRA rules. Ask for task description and confirmer. Qualified lawyers follow different route. Cite official guidance and date.
simulations.rubric: Authority; correct limitation; factual application; next steps.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: In-house triage
simulations.scenario: Fictional tech company receives three legal requests.
simulations.documents: Supplier renewal tomorrow; privacy incident reported this morning; marketing copy for next week. Incident severity unknown.
simulations.task: Prepare a prioritised action email with owners and next steps.
simulations.model: Escalate privacy incident immediately through incident process; establish scope/timeline and applicable obligations. Parallel assign supplier renewal, check commercial deadline and authority. Schedule marketing review. Communicate dependencies; no unsupported notification conclusion.
simulations.rubric: Urgency; incident response; delegation; clear communication.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Legal operations
simulations.scenario: Fictional legal team has 40 open matters.
simulations.documents: Ten high-priority matters have no owner; six deadlines in next week; several duplicates; sensitive details in free-text field.
simulations.task: Design a short matter tracker and review process.
simulations.model: Fields: matter ID, category, owner, priority, due date, stage, next action, authorised link; deduplicate and assign owners. Escalate imminent deadlines. Keep sensitive details in approved system; review turnaround and rework.
simulations.rubric: Data minimisation; owner/deadline; deduplication; quality metrics.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Professional conduct
simulations.scenario: Fictional trainee sends wrong draft to a client.
simulations.documents: Draft contains outdated fee clause and internal comments. Recipient has not responded.
simulations.model: Notify supervisor promptly; preserve accurate record; assess confidentiality and scope under policy. Agree correction/recall and communication; document actions and prevent repeat through version controls. Do not conceal or contact recipient contrary to instructions.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice or work experience.

simulations.title: Completion accounts — equity bridge and dispute
simulations.scenario: Fictional Northbridge buyer has agreed £120m enterprise value with a completion-accounts mechanism. Prepare a short note for the supervising associate (suggested time: 25 minutes). All amounts are in GBP millions.
simulations.documents: SPA extract: equity price = EV + cash − debt + (actual working capital − target working capital). Target working capital 14; cash 8; bank debt 25; actual working capital 11 before a disputed £2 overdue supplier invoice; the draft debt definition excludes ordinary trade payables. No other adjustments assumed. Seller excludes the invoice from working capital; buyer includes it as a current liability.
simulations.task: Calculate both parties' equity price; explain the disputed item and what evidence is needed; suggest the next step and avoid double-counting it as debt and working capital.
simulations.model: Seller calculation: 120 + 8 − 25 + (11 − 14) = £100m. Buyer calculation: actual working capital £9m after the £2m liability, so 120 + 8 − 25 + (9 − 14) = £98m. Difference £2m. Check whether invoice relates to pre-completion supply, accruals, underlying contracts, ledger and agreed accounting policies; confirm SPA definitions and dispute timetable. An overdue trade payable is not automatically financial debt. Avoid counting it in both categories. Escalate unresolved classification and preserve the disputed amount in the completion-accounts process; do not assert a final price before resolution.
simulations.rubric: 10 points: seller and buyer calculations 4; clear disputed item and double-count prevention 2; relevant evidence and accounting hierarchy 2; procedural next steps and caveat 2.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice, actual work experience or independently reviewed training.

simulations.title: Acquisition financing — covenant headroom and liquidity
simulations.scenario: Fictional borrower Elm Group is preparing a financing update. Suggested time: 30 minutes. Use only the simplified contractual assumptions provided; no external legal rules are necessary.
simulations.documents: Facility £80m, £50m drawn; no other debt; unrestricted cash £10m; LTM covenant EBITDA £20m. Net leverage covenant maximum 2.5x. A proposed £15m draw funds an immediate payment, leaving cash unchanged. Downside LTM EBITDA £17m. Facility requires no existing or resulting default at drawdown, subject to the terms. Ignore fees and other adjustments.
simulations.task: Calculate current leverage, pro forma leverage and downside leverage. Explain whether undrawn commitments equal usable liquidity, then propose a concise escalation plan.
simulations.model: Current net debt £40m; leverage 2.00x. After draw and spend, debt £65m, cash £10m, net debt £55m; leverage 2.75x, above 2.5x. Downside £55m/£17m = 3.24x. Current theoretical net debt ceiling £50m, headroom £10m before EBITDA changes. Undrawn £30m is not automatically available; verify exact test date, definitions, permitted adjustments, conditions, covenant cure and waivers with counsel. Escalate before draw; model smaller draw, equity injection or negotiated waiver. Do not say default has already occurred absent operative test mechanics.
simulations.rubric: 10 points: three ratios and headroom 4; distinction between commitment and availability 2; timing and documentation caveats 2; realistic mitigations and escalation 2.
simulations.notice: Original fictional exercise; not employer assessment, legal advice, actual work experience or independently reviewed training.

simulations.title: Legal research — source conflict and event chronology
simulations.scenario: Fictional retail merger: a partner needs a two-paragraph briefing before a client call. Suggested time: 20 minutes. The excerpts below are invented, not real documents.
simulations.documents: A. Issuer release 3 March: recommended offer announced, expected completion Q3 subject to conditions. B. Regulator update 4 June: Phase 1 concerns; undertakings may avoid reference. C. Issuer release 12 June: parties submitted remedies. D. Regulator update 18 June: regulator considers remedies potentially acceptable; consultation to follow. E. Trade newsletter 19 June: 'Deal cleared', cites D only.
simulations.task: Write a verified chronology and short client briefing, identify the misleading claim and explain whether the newsletter independently corroborates clearance.
simulations.model: 3 March announced; 4 June concerns; 12 June remedies submitted per parties; 18 June regulator considers potential acceptability, consultation pending. The latest primary regulator statement does not establish final acceptance or clearance. Newsletter is derivative of D and its interpretation conflicts with the source. simulations.title: Commercial contracts — obligation and remedy matrix
simulations.scenario: Fictional customer Finch Ltd is negotiating a software services renewal. Suggested time: 30 minutes. Produce a short negotiation matrix for counsel based on the following invented extracts.
simulations.documents: Annual fee £240,000. Availability target 99.9% monthly, excluding planned maintenance up to 6 hours. Credit 5% of monthly fee below 99.9%; 10% below 99.5%; credits stated exclusive remedy for availability failure. General liability cap 100% annual fee; confidentiality carve-out unclear. Supplier may appoint subprocessors with 10 days' notice; exit assistance available at unspecified rates. Customer requires data return within 30 days.
simulations.task: Calculate the credit at 99.4% assuming a full month and non-overlapping bands; identify four risks, proposed amendments, and priority. Explain unresolved points.
simulations.model: Monthly fee £20,000; 10% credit £2,000 at 99.4%, assuming applicable exclusions and non-cumulative bands. High: exclusive availability remedy may leave repeated material outages inadequately addressed; propose chronic failure termination and clarify bands. High: confidentiality exposure and ambiguous cap carve-out; clarify cap structure and negotiate proportionate treatment. High: subprocessor changes require data protection and contractual controls; propose objection/notification process and compliant terms where applicable. Medium/high: undefined exit fees and data return obligations; agree format, timelines, deletion and reasonable pre-agreed rates. Verify full contract, outage definition, governing law and customer risk appetite. This is negotiation analysis, not a legal enforceability opinion.
simulations.rubric: 10 points: calculation and assumptions 2; four risk-specific amendments 4; prioritisation 2; unresolved facts and caveats 2.
